findings.where: Hero, the headline "Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor" and the line under it ("Advice on … from a former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group…"), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The first screen never speaks in Mark's own voice. The headline is a name-and-role label, not a line Mark would say. The line under it describes him in the third person ("from a former Lead Lawyer"), the way a firm writes about its staff. The brief asks for Mark's own words in the headline, and for one strong line.
findings.who_objects: Mark, and the brief's client values 1, 3 and 6. Brand sheet §5 says the individual is the brand, and the copy should sound approachable rather than like a consultancy. The dualite carry-over puts his own words in the old-style headline. A development-bank officer meeting him for the first time hears a directory entry, not the advisor. This is the one thing this tile sets for every later round.

findings.where: Hero, the line under the headline, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does, but not who he does it for or where. Development banks, agencies and governments are not named, and neither are the regions of his work. A visitor can't tell in five seconds that this advisor works for organisations like theirs.
findings.who_objects: The audience in brand sheet §1: staff at multilateral development banks scanning for a consultant. First-visit trust items 2 and 6, and "what a visitor must be sure of": that he has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs, in their region. The article specimen shows Mark's real copy already mentions development-agency clients, so this needs no new claim.

findings.where: Hero, "Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience", desktop and phone
findings.fault: The proof next to the one action is a size word (a count of years). The checkable fact right beside it, the World Bank PPP Group role, carries more weight on its own.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded reader at a development bank, who judges an advisor on the kind of project, the role and the region, not on years claimed (first-visit trust, "Feel the CV": never size words such as "40 years of experience"). It also leans towards the big-firm boast that client value 6 rules out.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the principle words "precise, light, quick" and the easing note "brisk out of rest", with the headline as the element that enters, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The motion character the tile sets is brisk, and the first thing it moves is text. The brief's motion value is calm first: one quiet picture or moment before any text asks for anything. "Quick" sets the opposite tone for the animation round to build within.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the brief's client value 2 (the Threlfall take Mark liked: the picture first, the words after). The animation round (#9) would inherit a quick, text-first motion language that works against the calm opening he asked for.

findings.where: Style tile, the "Type pair" row at desktop width: Gelasio in the left column, Source Sans 3 alone in the right column
findings.fault: The pair is split across the wide gutter. Only the left half has the "Type pair" label, and only the right column's sections (Texture, Motion sketch) have a rule under the label. So Source Sans 3 reads as a separate, unlabelled item in the right column, not as the second half of a pair. Proximity and similarity group the page by column, not by section.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, reading the tile to judge whether the two faces work together, and the layout round, which reads the tile as its spec. The pairing is the point of the row, and the arrangement pulls it apart.
